match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the definitions of health (absence of disease versus the WHO's complete physical, mental and social wellbeing); the closest, on health being dynamic and subjective, teaches a different idea, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Definitions of health
card: health is the absence of disease, illness or injury. It looks only at the body and treating what is wrong.
the World Health Organization defines health as a state of complete physical, mental and social wellbeing, and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.
The WHO definition is wider because it counts mental and social wellbeing, not only the body. A person with no disease may still not be healthy under it.
Some people criticise the word complete, as few people would ever reach it. Even so, the WHO definition is widely used.
draft.remember: Health can mean no disease, or wellbeing in body, mind and social life.

a.q: Which statement best matches the WHO definition of health?
opts: Physical, mental and social wellbeing, not just no disease
Being free from disease, illness and injury
Being physically fit and able to play sport
Having access to doctors and hospitals when ill
a.why: The WHO definition includes physical, mental and social wellbeing. Being free from disease is the biomedical view, which is tempting but leaves out mental and social wellbeing.
a.clue: The WHO goes beyond the body alone.

b.q: Jin has no illness or injury, but he feels lonely and has no close friends since moving to Geelong. How would each definition describe his health?
opts: Biomedical: healthy. WHO: not fully healthy
Biomedical: not healthy. WHO: not fully healthy
Biomedical: healthy. WHO: fully healthy
Biomedical: not healthy. WHO: fully healthy
b.why: The biomedical view looks only for disease, illness or injury, and Jin has none. The WHO view includes social wellbeing, so his loneliness means he is not fully healthy. The second option is tempting, but the biomedical view does not count loneliness.
b.clue: Which definition counts loneliness as part of health?

a.best: Physical, mental and social wellbeing, not just no disease

b.best: Biomedical: healthy. WHO: not fully healthy
